data.one_liner: Build widgets depending on image dimensions and pixel colors.
data.what_it_does: Allows you to extend the background color of an image to match its edges, or build custom widgets depending on an image's width, height, and pixel colors.
use_when: You need to dynamically match a container's background color to an image's edge pixels.
You need to read pixel colors or dimensions of an image within a widget builder.
You want to detect tapped pixel colors on an image using a GestureDetector.
avoid_when: You only need basic image loading and caching without pixel manipulation.
You are performing heavy real-time image processing operations on large video streams.
strengths: Provides direct access to image pixel colors and dimensions via an easy builder pattern.
Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
weaknesses: Not documented for heavy, performant off-screen image manipulation at scale.
data.setup_notes: No special native permissions or build steps required.

alternatives.name: cached_network_image
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you primarily need to load and cache network images with placeholders and error handling rather than inspecting pixel colors.

alternatives.name: image
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a comprehensive Dart library for image decoding, encoding, and heavy image manipulation outside of the widget tree.

data.minimal_example:
ImagePixels(
    imageProvider: imageProvider,
    defaultColor: Colors.grey,
    builder: (context, img) => Text("Img size is: ${img.width} × ${img.height}"),
)
